messages:
kevin: Quick q — thinking about a 'config reservoir' concept to safely roll out high-cardinality runtime flags (per-customer routing + quota overrides). We need an eviction policy for the reservoir when memory limit is hit. Options: LRU per-team, TTL, or size-based probabilistic eviction. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

liz: love the term 'reservoir' :) Can you sketch the load pattern? Is it mostly long tail (many tiny tenants) or a few heavy customers? That changes the approach. :eyes:

kevin: mostly long tail. 80/20 but tail is huge — thousands of tiny tenant overrides. We can't load all into RAM for private deploys. Need deterministic fallback to global config to avoid noisy failures.

nate: we already use segmented LRU for KV caches. For configs I'd lean TTL + admission control + bloom filter to reduce thundering herd on cache miss. TTL default 1h, bump for active tenants.

sara (eng-platform): +1 for bounce protection. Also need telemetry: emit metric on-eviction with eviction_reason and an anonymized sample (hashed tenant ids), and a per-shard occupancy gauge.

liz: UX: console should show reservoir occupancy per shard and a top-20 tail list (hashed ids) and a 'pin' control so support/product can pin paid customers into the reservoir.

kevin: also important: if eviction removes an override we should route to a deterministic fallback policy (e.g., route-by-policy => prefer stable model variants) rather than returning error. No 5xx on miss.

deploy-bot: deploy started: config-reservoir-v1 -> canary (5%) — 1919002000

nate: testing notes: need a harness that simulates tail churn and admission thresholds. Also suggest a safety gate: if eviction_rate > 1% for >5m, automatically rollback canary.

liz: what about probabilistic admission? only admit overrides if tenant had >N requests in last T minutes, else use global config. That reduces memory pressure.

kevin: careful — that skews new customers. Maybe combine with billing: auto-pin on first paid request or when support toggles pin.

sara (eng-platform): I'll draft an RFC with metrics, circuit-breaker thresholds, and rollout playbook. Will post link in a bit.

kevin: also, here's a small config prototype for eviction policy so we have something concrete when drafting the RFC:

```
eviction_policy: {
  type: "ttl_with_lru",
  ttl_seconds: 3600,
  lru_segments: 16,
  admission_threshold: {
    requests: 5,
    window_seconds: 300
  },
  pin_label: "billing:paid"
}
```

liz: nice and explicit. I'll wire console controls and telemetry panels to these fields. :thumbsup:

kevin: OK starting canary at 1919002222 — monitoring eviction_rate, miss_rate, and p95 latency. Ping if you see spikes.

nate: noted — I'll add synthetic tests and a canary monitor to the alerting runbook.
